5: The Yerushalmi [says] immediately [juxtapose] redemption [to prayer] etc. in the first chapter of Berakhot: And it is written in the glosses of the Asheri on the first chapter of Berakhot that on Shabbat one need not juxtapose redemption to prayer, since we derive it from "May the Lord answer you on a day of trouble" (Psalms 20:2), and it is written after it "May the words of my mouth [be acceptable]" (Psalms 19:15), and Shabbat is not a day of trouble—thus far [his words]. But his words do not seem correct, because that verse is merely an asmakhta (support), and even without that verse one must juxtapose redemption to prayer. And furthermore, the Shabbat prayer is in place of the weekday prayer, which is supplication in time of trouble
